'''''Hippeastrum aulicum''''', the '''Lily of the Palace''',  is a [[bulb]]ous [[perennial]], in the family [[Amaryllidaceae]], native to the [[Atlantic Forest]] and [[Cerrado]] [[ecoregions]] from [[Brazil]] to [[Paraguay]], in [[South America]].

==Description==
[[File:Immature Hippeastrum aulicum (Ker Gawl.) Herb. bulb.jpg|thumb|Immature ''Hippeastrum aulicum'' (Ker Gawl.) Herb. bulb]]
''Hippeastrum aulicum'' is a bulbous [[epiphyte]], growing on rocks and trees which has large scarlet flowers with a green throat, usually with four flowers to a stem. It blooms in late summer and autumn.<ref name=PBS>[http://www.pacificbulbsociety.org/pbswiki/index.php/Hippeastrum_aulicum Pacific Bulb Society: ''Hippeastrum aulicum'']</ref>

== Taxonomy ==
''Hippeastrum aulicum'' was first described by [[Ker Gawler]] in 1883.<ref name=KewWC/><ref name=Trop>{{cite web|title=Hippeastrum aulicum|url=http://www.tropicos.org/Name/1200034|work=Tropicos|publisher=[[Missouri Botanical Gardens]]|accessdate=19 March 2014}}</ref>

=== Etymology ===
The species name ''aulicum'' comes from the Latin, meaning 'princely'.<ref>{{cite web|last=Griffith|first=Chuck|title=Dictionary of Botanical Epithets|url=http://www.winternet.com/~chuckg/dictionary/dictionary.34.html|accessdate=19 March 2014|date=2005}}</ref>

==Cultivation==
''Hippeastrum aulicum'' is cultivated by specialty flower bulb nurseries as an [[ornamental plant]].<ref>[http://fortheloveofbulbs.blogspot.com/2011/11/hippeastrum-aulicum-epiphytic-species.html "For The Love Of Bulbs" Blog:  ''Hippeastrum aulicum''] . accessed 11.28.2013</ref>
